sentences.text: This Writ Petition has been filed for the issue of writ of mandamus directing the respondents to withdraw / drop the acquisition proceedings and to reconvey the lands that were acquired from the petitioners by considering the representation made by the petitioner on 11.09.2020.

sentences.text: 3. The case of the petitioners is that they had purchased the subject property through a registered sale deed dated 04.09.2019 registered as Document No.3294 of 2019.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: The petitioners came to know that the National Highways have proceeded to include the subject property during the acquisition proceedings.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: According to the petitioners, neither the petitioners nor their vendors have received any compensation amount and that apart, the land that was acquired has not been utilized.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioners made a representation for reconveyance of the subject property.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: Since the same was not considered, the present writ petition has been filed before this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: 4. In the considered view of this Court, if the compensation amount has not been received by the petitioners or their vendors, it has to be independently agitated by the petitioners in the manner known to law.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: That cannot be a ground to seek for the reconveyance of the land.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: Even in the counter affidavit that has been filed by the National Highways https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Department, it is stated that the compensation amount has been paid to the vendors of the petitioners.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: It is not necessary for this Court to go into this issue.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: The only issue that requires consideration of this Court is as to whether the petitioners are entitled for reconveyance of the land that was acquired under the National Highways Act and it has been repeatedly held that there is no provision under the National Highways Act for reconveyance of the acquired land to the land owners.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: The law on this issue is no longer res integra.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Useful reference can be made to the Judgment of this Court in the case of G.Poosanam Vs. the Project Director,
National Highways Authority of India, No.7E, 5th Cross Jakkappan Nagar, Krishnagiri and others in W.P.16186 of 2011 dated 16.09.2020.

entities.text:

National Highways Authority of India, No.7E, 5th Cross Jakkappan Nagar, Krishnagiri and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: In the absence of any specific provision under the Act, there is no scope for the respondents to reconvey the lands that have been acquired.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

sentences.text: This Court cannot issue any directions beyond the scope of the National Highways Act and hence, the relief sought for by the petitioners cannot be granted by this Court.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 12 October, 2023.json

 JUDGMENT (Judgment of the Court was delivered by S.SRIMATHY, J.) The present writ appeal is filed by the writ petitioner against the order dated 12.10.2023 passed in W.P.(MD)No.4085 of 2021.

2. The writ petition was filed for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus, to direct the respondents to withdraw / drop the petitioner's land situated in Survey Nos.1/14A1, 3/12A of Vilacheri Village,
Nagamalaipudukkottai, Madurai District, measuring an extent of 22.5 cents from the additional land acquisition proceedings.

sentences.text: 3. The case of the writ petitioners is that they had purchased the subject property through a Registered Sale Deed in document No.3294 of 2019, dated 04.09.2019.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: The petitioners came to know about the acquisition proceedings but neither the petitioners nor their vendors have received any compensation.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Further, the land acquired has not been utilized.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioners submitted a representation for reconveyance of the subject property.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Hence, the writ petition was filed.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: 4. After considering the rival claims, the Writ Court had held if compensation is not received, it has to be independently agitated by the petitioners in a manner known to law and the same cannot be a ground for re- conveyancing the land.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Further held under the National Highways Act, there is no provision for re-conveying the land to the land owners and dismissed the writ petition.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Aggrieved over the same the writ petitioner had filed the present writ appeal.

Mr.S.S.Madhavan, the learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the respondents 2 and 3 and Mr.P.Karthick, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 5th respondent and perused the records.
6.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: The primary contention of the appellant / writ petitioner is that they did not receive any compensation for the acquisition of their lands.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: The respondents have filed counter wherein it has been categorically stated that the writ petitioners' vendors have received the compensation.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: On perusing the sale deed, it is seen that one R.Meenakshi is the petitioners' vendor.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: In the counter the respondents have stated that the said R.Meenakshi had received compensation under 3D Main Award dated 05.04.2007 which was quantified as Rs.32,283/- and the same was disbursed vide cheque No.208027 dated 23.07.2007.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text:
However, the said vendor did not turn up for 3G enquiry,
hence the said vendor did not receive the compensation under 3G Additional Award, dated 26.06.2009.
7.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Further it is seen that the 3D Main Award was on 05.04.2007 and the 3G Additional Award was on 26.06.2009.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: But the sale executed by the said vendor to the writ petitioner was on 04.09.2019.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: The sale deed is executed nearly after 12 years after the Main Award and 10 years of Additional Award.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Furthermore, in the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 21/04/2025 12:00:11 pm ) said sale deed it is mentioned that National Highway Authority had acquired 1008 square meters.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the writ petitioners plea cannot be entertained since the sale is subsequent to the award proceedings.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: 8. If at all aggrieved by non-payment of award, then it is the original owner who would be aggrieved and not the appellant / writ petitioner who had purchased the remaining lands after land acquisition proceedings.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: In other words, the petitioner cannot step into the shoes of the original owner and claim the compensation is not paid, hence reconvey the land, when the petitioner is not having any privity of contract with the National Highways Authority at all.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the Writ Court has rightly rejected the plea of the writ petitioner.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text:
9. Further it is the specific contention of the respondents that there is no provision for re-conveying the land to the land owners under National Highways Act and the said issue was already decided in the case of G.Poosanam Vs. the Project Director, National Highways Authority of India, in W.P.No.16186 of 2011, dated 16.09.2020.

sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: Under section 3J of National Highways Act it is stated that Nothing in the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 shall apply to an acquisition under this Act.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: The effect of it is that the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is not applicable, hence reconveying it not available.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text:
But the said section 3J is struck down by the Courts and the effect of it would be Land Acquisition Act,
1894 is applicable and the reconveying of land is available to National Highways Act.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: After hearing the rival submissions, this Court is of the considered opinion that the appellant has not locus standi to claim reconvey the land since the lands were not acquired from the appellants.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: The lands were acquired from the original owner R.Meenakshi and compensation was paid to the original owner.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: As held supra, if at all there is a claim it is the original owner who has to claim and not the appellant, since the land was acquired from the original owner and award was granted in the year 2007 and 2009, but the appellant had purchased the land in the year 2019.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: 12. Further at the time of acquisition proceedings the section 3J was in existence, but the same was struck down on a later date.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Therefore, any https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
21/04/2025 12:00:11 pm ) transaction which was completed cannot be reopened.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Therefore,
considering from any angle the appellant is not having any legally sustainable ground.
13.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: However, the question of law raised in this case is left open, as and when the original owner is claiming such relief the same will be considered in accordance to law.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: 14. Therefore, the writ appeal is liable to be dismissed and accordingly dismissed.
sentences._hearing_file: J.Balamurugan vs The Union Of India on 8 April, 2025.json

sentences.text: No costs.

opennyai_summary.12_October_2023__facts:
According to the petitioners, neither the petitioners nor their vendors have received any compensation amount and that apart, the land that was acquired has not been utilized.
Therefore, the petitioners made a representation for reconveyance of the subject property.
Since the same was not considered, the present writ petition has been filed before this Court.
opennyai_summary.12_October_2023__ANALYSIS:
4. In the considered view of this Court, if the compensation amount has not been received by the petitioners or their vendors, it has to be independently agitated by the petitioners in the manner known to law.
That cannot be a ground to seek for the reconveyance of the land.
In the absence of any specific provision under the Act, there is no scope for the respondents to reconvey the lands that have been acquired.
opennyai_summary.12_October_2023__decision:
This Court cannot issue any directions beyond the scope of the National Highways Act and hence, the relief sought for by the petitioners cannot be granted by this Court.
Accordingly, the Writ Petition stands dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
Therefore, the petitioners submitted a representation for reconveyance of the subject property.
Hence, the writ petition was filed.
Further held under the National Highways Act, there is no provision for re-conveying the land to the land owners and dismissed the writ petition.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The primary contention of the appellant / writ petitioner is that they did not receive any compensation for the acquisition of their lands.
The respondents have filed counter wherein it has been categorically stated that the writ petitioners' vendors have received the compensation.
In the counter the respondents have stated that the said R.Meenakshi had received compensation under 3D Main Award dated 05.04.2007 which was quantified as Rs.32,283/- and the same was disbursed vide cheque No.208027 dated 23.07.2007.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
However, the said vendor did not turn up for 3G enquiry,
hence the said vendor did not receive the compensation under 3G Additional Award, dated 26.06.2009.
7.
In other words, the petitioner cannot step into the shoes of the original owner and claim the compensation is not paid, hence reconvey the land, when the petitioner is not having any privity of contract with the National Highways Authority at all.
Therefore, the Writ Court has rightly rejected the plea of the writ petitioner.
Under section 3J of National Highways Act it is stated that Nothing in the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 shall apply to an acquisition under this Act.
The effect of it is that the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is not applicable, hence reconveying it not available.
But the said section 3J is struck down by the Courts and the effect of it would be Land Acquisition Act,
1894 is applicable and the reconveying of land is available to National Highways Act.
The lands were acquired from the original owner R.Meenakshi and compensation was paid to the original owner.
As held supra, if at all there is a claim it is the original owner who has to claim and not the appellant, since the land was acquired from the original owner and award was granted in the year 2007 and 2009, but the appellant had purchased the land in the year 2019.
12. Further at the time of acquisition proceedings the section 3J was in existence, but the same was struck down on a later date.
